title: Steady a swinging conveyor carrier before lifting a tin out of it
instruction: The hanging carrier is swinging. Steady it, then lift the open tin out, stand it on the green pad and let go.
context: Parts on finishing, plating and assembly lines ride in baskets hung from overhead conveyors, and a carrier swings after it stops or is bumped. The worker steadies it by hand before unloading, so the part is not snatched out of a moving basket or knocked over. Done by: conveyor operators and tenders (O*NET 53-7011.00), hand packers (53-7064.00). Unlike TK-Y3Z9U9 and TK-PXVVWY, this task requires catching and stopping a swinging container by hand before taking its load out.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Hanging carrier (moving part 0.30 kg, its centre of mass directly below the pivot): an open orange plastic basket, 110 x 110 mm outside, 5 mm walls and floor, centred 30.0 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline, its floor's underside 25 mm and its rim 65 mm above the table; a grab tab (orange plastic, 70 mm long, 20 mm wide, 10 mm thick) sticks straight out of the middle of the robot-side wall toward the robot, its top flush with the rim (55 to 65 mm high); a balancing bar (orange plastic, 20 x 110 x 26 mm) runs along the inside foot of the robot-side wall, 23 to 49 mm high. The basket hangs from dark steel rods 8 mm across: two short horizontal rods from the middle of the far wall (away from the robot) to a vertical rod 11.5 cm beyond the basket centre, away from the robot (at 36 and 59 mm high), the vertical rod from 30 to 550 mm high, and a top rod from it back toward the robot to the pivot, directly above the basket centre at 550 mm, with a pivot boss 16 mm across and 24 mm long. The pivot axis runs left-right, so the carrier swings toward and away from the robot. Stand (fixed, grey steel): a 100 x 100 x 10 mm base plate and a 30 x 30 mm post 570 mm tall, centred 57.0 cm in front of the arm bases on the midline, and a 16 x 16 mm arm from the post top toward the robot to the pivot, 26 mm left of the midline, carrying an 8 mm axle into the pivot. Tin (loose, blue painted steel, 60 g, open top): a cylinder 30 mm across and 90 mm tall, standing upright in the centre of the basket floor; it stands 55 mm above the rim, and tips over if pushed sideways at about a third of g. Pad (fixed, green rubber disc): 80 mm across, 4 mm thick, centred 20.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 20.0 cm left of the midline. Start: at time zero the carrier passes through hanging, moving away from the robot at 0.90 rad/s with the tin moving with it, so it swings about 11.7 degrees each way (the basket about 10 cm each way) with a period of 1.43 s; left alone it still swings 10.3 degrees each way after 45 s.
scoring: Measure from the video and a photo. Steady: over the last 1.5 s the carrier swings less than 2 degrees either side (half its peak-to-peak swing angle). On the pad and let go: the tin stands within 10 degrees of upright, still, its base within 2 mm of the pad's top surface, its centre within 25 mm of the pad's centre, and no part of either gripper within 5 mm of it. Score 1.0: tin on the pad and let go, and the carrier steady. Score 0.5: the tin was lifted out while the carrier was steady and stands on the pad, let go, but the carrier is swinging 2 degrees or more at the end. Score 0 otherwise, and 0 for the whole trial if at any time: the tin tips more than 20 degrees from the basket's vertical while in the basket, or from vertical once out of it; the tin's lowest point comes within 2 mm of the table top; or the tin is out of the basket (its centre beyond the basket's inside wall faces, or its base above the rim) and more than 6 mm above the table while the carrier swings 2 degrees or more. A trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the last step.
reset_notes: Put the tin back upright in the centre of the basket floor and let the carrier hang still, then start it swinging: in the simulator it is given 0.90 rad/s through the hanging position, away from the robot, at time zero (on a real rig, pull the basket 11.7 degrees toward the robot and let it go 0.36 s, a quarter swing, before the trial starts). The whole-trial failure records are cleared only by this scene reset. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate, scaled down: rigid boxes and cylinders, a 110 mm basket and a 60 g tin on a 0.30 kg carrier. The pivot is a free hinge whose damping is set so the swing decays as slowly as on a ball-bearing pivot (11.7 to 10.3 degrees in 45 s). The tin is a solid cylinder: tipping is scored, spilling is not simulated. The start swing is set as a velocity at time zero. The start is fixed, so a memorised catch time cannot be ruled out.
